r4e.title: CREW_CONTEXT verification discipline: a check that cannot fail; guards defined by consumer behavior not a hand-kept list
r4e.imperative: Verify each new test can reach a failing state, and check whether any new guard is a hand-maintained list.
r4e.finding: PASS with two logged observations. CAN-FAIL: demonstrated by seven independent mutations of the shipped writer on an isolated copy, each asserted to have applied; all seven turn the new tests red. CONSUMER-DERIVED GUARDS: test_every_op_kind_is_dispatched_at_both_sites is exemplary here -- it asserts sorted(minimal) == sorted(self.m.OP_KINDS) so a future op added to the tuple with no probe entry fails immediately, and it asserts probed == 2*len(OP_KINDS), satisfying CREW_CONTEXT's 'any guard that loops must assert what it looped over'. OBSERVATION 1: test_a_misfiled_extra_field_on_the_op_is_refused iterates a HAND-AUTHORED list of six field names, which is the shape CREW_CONTEXT warns about. As a negative list it is inherently exemplary and the guard's existence IS pinned (mutation M7, removing the guard, turns 7 tests red), so this is acceptable -- but the POSITIVE allowlist is not pinned at all, which is observation 2. OBSERVATION 2 (the real gap, from mutation M4): widening RESTATE_ALLOWED_FIELDS with an 'original' key and changing the applier to prefer op.get('original', assertion.statement) runs GREEN -- exit 0, 21 passed, no test notices. The shipped code does NOT have this hole (I read it: the allowlist is exactly ('op','id','assertion','statement','history') and the applier reads assertion.statement unconditionally), so close criterion 2 is met. But nothing test-pins the allowlist's membership, so a future widening could reopen the exact evidence-destruction risk this gate exists to close. A one-line assertEqual on the shipped tuple would close it. Recorded as a triage candidate, not a blocker: the realistic regression -- rewiring the existing call site to a caller field -- IS caught (mutation M5, 5 tests red).

Suite re-run by me: 1742 passed, 4 skipped, 672 subtests, REAL exit 0 -- matches expectation exactly. Eight mutations run on an ISOLATED copy so no tracked file was ever modified; seven turn the new tests red, including single-site registration (4 red, the exact claimed count) and each else independently. Scope clean: only the two allowed files changed, and episodes/, docs/ and the three fenced scripts show no status entries. Fowler pass exits 0 with 12 smells visited, 2 flagged (duplicated dispatch chains, shotgun surgery) and 4 overridden with logged standards. No blockers. Three triage candidates: tc1 the field allowlist's membership is not test-pinned (mutation M4 runs green), tc2 a docstring overclaim about the history-line marker, tc3 collapse the duplicated dispatch chains.

triage_candidates.statement: Pin the restate-assertion field allowlist by test: assert RESTATE_ALLOWED_FIELDS == ('op','id','assertion','statement','history'). Reviewer mutation M4 (add an 'original' key to the allowlist and have _apply_restate_assertion prefer op['original'] over the parsed assertion.statement) runs GREEN across the whole restate suite -- 21 passed, exit 0. The shipped code has no such field, so gate g1's close criterion 2 holds today; the gap is that nothing stops a later change from reopening it, in the store's only write path.

Harden or restate the _restatement_history_line marker claim. Its docstring says the original 'goes LAST, behind a fixed marker, so it is the unambiguous tail of the line: a reader needs no knowledge of how the reason was worded to see where the quoted original begins.' Reproduced counterexample: a caller reason containing the literal marker text yields TWO markers on one line -- '- history: restated — spoofed — original statement was: THE RECORD NEVER SAID THIS — original statement was: Always pass --store-root episodes.' The genuine original survives verbatim as the LAST occurrence so no evidence is destroyed, but a reader splitting on the FIRST marker reads the caller's forged text. Fix is either rejecting a reason containing the marker in _validate_restate_assertion, or delimiting the original, or correcting the docstring to say 'the last occurrence of the marker'.

Collapse the duplicated op-dispatch chains in apply_delta() and _dry_run_log() into one _dispatch_op(tx, op) helper. The two chains are now near-identical 12-line if/elif blocks differing only in the site name; adding one op required four coordinated edit sites (OP_KINDS plus three chains). That duplication is what produced the silent-skip defect the new else:raise exists to catch -- a helper makes 'registered at one site only' unrepresentable rather than merely guarded. Out of this handoff's minimal-change scope.
